summary: media types missing ['application/3gpp-json-patch+json', 'application/json-patch+json']; media types extra ['application/vnd.3gpp.json-patch+json']; 4 absent, 3 extra

answer.why_different: The generated document appears to combine information from a different 3GPP version or media-type naming convention, while also changing the request-body schema structure and incorrectly moving a responses block inside requestBody. The differences involve changed values (description and media type), changed schema structure, and an invalid structural address for responses.
answer.spec_3gpp: The specification requires four PATCH media types. It specifies Resource for merge-patch bodies and array(PatchItem) for JSON Patch bodies. It also uses the vendor media-type spelling application/vnd.3gpp.json-patch+json in the operation mapping.
answer.openapi: OpenAPI request bodies use content entries whose keys are media types and whose values provide a schema. A Request Body Object has fields such as description, required, and content; responses belong to the operation, not inside requestBody. The generated requestBody therefore is not valid OpenAPI 3.0 because it contains responses.
answer.clearer_why: The official request body description explicitly lists all supported patch media types and their standards, and its schemas directly show the expected payload type for each media type. The generated version omits that explanation, omits two required media types, and contains an invalid nested responses block.

citations.quote: Four patch media types are available for the request message body.
The following patch media types are available:
content | Map[`string`, [Media Type Object](#media-type-object)] | REQUIRED. The content of the request body.

differences.reason: The generated side removes the request-body description, which loses the explicit explanation of the supported media types and their standards. This information is present in the official side and is supported by the specification, so the omission loses information rather than merely rewording it. The ruling relies on C1 and S1.

For application/3gpp-merge-patch+json, the official schema directly references Resource, matching the specification's stated request body type. Replacing that reference with a different schema structure loses the direct Resource constraint. The ruling relies on C1 and S1.

The added oneOf permits an array of Resource for application/3gpp-merge-patch+json, whereas the operation mapping specifies this media type as having request body type Resource. This is an unsupported widening of the accepted payload structure. The ruling relies on C2 and S1.

The generated side omits application/json-patch+json, one of the four media types explicitly required by the specification, and therefore loses a supported request representation. The ruling relies on S1, S2, and C1.

The generated side omits application/3gpp-json-patch+json, which the specification explicitly lists as an available media type with an array(PatchItem) body. This is a missing supported API representation. The ruling relies on S1, S2, and C1.

Although it differs from the official document, application/vnd.3gpp.json-patch+json is the media-type spelling explicitly given in the operation-mapping specification, and its array of PatchItem schema matches the specified body type. Thus this generated entry is better supported by the supplied specification than the official application/3gpp-json-patch+json entry. The ruling relies on S1 and C2.

The generated side adds responses under requestBody, but the supplied validation result states that this is not a valid OpenAPI 3.0 field and the generated block also contains an unresolved ErrorResponsePatch reference. This is a structural error, not merely an extra response definition. The ruling relies on C2 and O1.

evidence.text:
12.1.1.4 Data type definitions › 12.1.1.4.1a Structured data types

###### 12.1.1.4.1a.4 Type MoiChange (part 4/8)

The properties \"op\", \"path\" and \"value\" shall use the 3GPP JSON
Patch format (TS 32.158 \[15\]) for reporting NRM changes. The \"merge\"
operation specified by 3GPP JSON Patch is not supported in
\"notifyMOIChanges\". The \"move\", \"copy\" and \"test\" operations
specified by JSON Patch are not supported either.

The \"oldValue\" is an optional extension for \"notifyMOIChanges\"
allowing to report also the value that the attribute had before
replacing the value with the new value, that is contained in \"value\".

The following example notification (where JSON is expressed in YAML
notation) reports an object creation

href: https://example.com/3gpp

\...

moiChanges

\- notificationId: 123456789

op: add

path: /ClassA=1

value:

id: 1,

objectClass: ClassA,

attributes:

attrA: 123

attrB:

subAttrB1: ABC

subAttrB2: 56

The following example reports the deletion of that object.

href: https://example.com/3gpp

\...

moiChanges

\- notificationId: 123456789

op: remove

path: /ClassA=1

The following example reports the addition of a new attribute \"attrC\".

href: https://example.com/3gpp

\...

moiChanges

\- notificationId: 123456789

op: add

path: /ClassA=1\#/attributes/attrC

value: xyz

The following example reports the deletion of the attribute \"attrC\".

href: https://example.com/3gpp

\...

moiChanges

\- notificationId: 123456789

op: remove

path: /ClassA=1\#/attributes/attrC

The following example reports a value change for the simple attribute
\"attrA\".

href: https://example.com/3gpp

\...

moiChanges

\- notificationId: 123456789

op: replace

path: /ClassA=1\#/attributes/attrA

value: 456

When the old value is reported as well, the notification looks like.

href: https://example.com/3gpp

\...

moiChanges

\- notificationId: 123456789

op: replace

path: /ClassA=1\#/attributes/attrA

value: 456

oldValue: 123

The following example reports a value change for the complex attribute
\"attrB\".

href: https://example.com/3gpp

\...

moiChanges

\- notificationId: 123456789

op: replace

path: /ClassA=1\#/attributes/attrB

value:

subAttrB1: abc

subAttrB2: 78

The previous two notifications can be combined into a single
notification as follows.

href: https://example.com/3gpp

\...

moiChanges

\- notificationId: 123456789

op: replace

path: /ClassA=1\#/attributes/attrA

value: 456

\- notificationId: 123456789

op: replace

path: /ClassA=1\#/attributes/attrB

value:

subAttrB1: abc

subAttrB2: 78

Note the operation \"replace\" has replace semantics and not merge
semantics. The following notification reports the value change of the
attribute field \"attrB:subAttrB1\" to \"def\" and the deletion of the
attribute field \"attrB:subAttrB2\".

href: https://example.com/3gpp

\...

moiChanges

\- notificationId: 123456789

op: replace

path: /ClassA=1\#/attributes/attrB

value:

subAttrB1: def

The value change of the attribute field \"attrA:subAttrB1\" is reported
as follows.

href: https://example.com/3gpp

\...

moiChanges

\- notificationId: 123456789

op: replace

path: /ClassA=1\#/attributes/attrA/subAttrB1

value: def

Assume \"attrD\" is a JSON array with simple elements, then the creation
of this multi-valued attribute is reported as follows.

href: https://example.com/3gpp

\...

moiChanges

\- notificationId: 123456789

op: add

path: /ClassA=1\#/attributes/attrD

value:

\- 1

\- 2

\- 3

Its deletion is reported by the following notification.

href: https://example.com/3gpp

\...

moiChanges

\- notificationId: 123456789

op: remove

path: /ClassA=1\#/attributes/attrD

The complete replacement of the array is reported by the following
notification.

href: https://example.com/3gpp

\...

moiChanges

\- notificationId: 123456789

op: add

path: /ClassA=1\#/attributes/attrD

value:

\- 11

\- 21

\- 31

A document (or set of documents) that defines or describes an API. An OpenAPI definition uses and conforms to the OpenAPI Specification.  
##### Path Templating
Path templating refers to the usage of curly braces ({}) to mark a section of a URL path as replaceable using path parameters.  
##### Media Types
Media type definitions are spread across several resources.
The media type definitions SHOULD be in compliance with [RFC6838](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6838).
